The Cerro Cathedral is a place of incredible beauty, really a must for those who visit Bariloche. However, during the high season, the queues to buy the cable car tickets can be quite long, which makes you waste a good time.

There is the online purchase option, and the value (both presencial and digital) is 36.000 Argentine pesos. However, it is worth noting that even buying in advance there is no guarantee of access, since everything depends on the climatic conditions. Therefore, my tip is: program to face the queue on site, but always checking first if the cable cars are working.

An important detail is that the park’s app itself tells you in real time which lifts are active, a feature that can save time and avoid frustrations.

For those who do not want to spend with a tourist agency, there are line buses that take to the Cerro and make the journey back. Just keep an eye on the schedule. The cost is less than 1000 Argentine pesos, which represents a great economy.

The highest peak in the surroundings of Bariloche and the only one which snow and ice cover the ground throughout the year.  Stunning beyond words.  I took so many photographs.  The scenery was spectacular.  Beautiful drive to get there.  Easy relaxing walk at the base, anyone can do it.  We had the perfect winter day.  Crispy but warm with sunny blue skies. We took the “Dos Glacieres” tour from El Chalten. It gets you out of the “normal” national park area to the north to explore a different area. The 2 glaciers are Vespignani and Huemul. You get almost 3 hours to explore the area around Veapignani and 2 hours to hike up to Huemul … so lots of walking opportunities. Huemul is particularly beautiful. At a very reasonable price this is a tour worth doing. Back in El Chalten at 5pm so a full day.

My elderly in-laws went on the “One Shot VESPIGNANI” package with transfer from El Chalten included. My father-in-law wanted to see a lake in the area but was able to do the long hikes around El Chalten, so we thought this lake tour would be great for him. 

The tour comprised a bus ride from El Chalten to the ferry, a ferry ride, and then some time to putz around at the glacier area (apparently they did a 600+ ft elevation gain hike in 1.5 hours, which we were stunned as they are not youn…). They bought last minute tickets - we had WhatsApp-ed the company in the morning to check if there were seats available for the same day tour (the website won’t allow you to buy tickets too close to the tour but it doesn’t mean the tour is sold out), then walked over to their office to pay. 

The bus came to pick them up from our accomodation. They left town at 11am and were back in town around 5.15pm. We were worried they would get motion sickness on the bus, get cold, fall off the ferry and die of hypothermia, break an ankle, get hungry, etc. but they came back raving about what a wonderful and magnificent time they had and their only complaint was they felt it was a bit rushed. 

We looked at their photos and videos and it looked like they got a really great experience typical of hiking in Patagonia for less physical effort than if they attempted the trails from El Chalten.

The excursion itself is beautiful and priced accordingly. The places are wonderful but many points to improve. To begin with, the guide that guides absolutely nothing and spent the entire round trip chatting with a friend. Everyone in the transfer aware of his love life. The van on the way there was very nice and the driver on the way there was very professional, but on the way back the van fell apart. Upon returning, the guide did not count the passengers before leaving and halfway there they called them by radio to return to look for the forgotten pax. The driver made a sudden turn and collided with a tree. Horror!! Furthermore, he drove fast and although the road is very bad, he was very rough. Nothing to do with the driver on the way. The dome lacks a lot of love. It was dirty, neglected. On the other hand, the boat was very clean and the sailors were very helpful. I would go again but there are definitely things that could be improved to increase the quality of the excursion.

We took this excursion for a day in El Chaltén and overall had a great time.  The lake is beautiful and the trails available are fantastic. The trip starts with a bus ride to the lake which is about an hour along the river. Then a 30 minute boat ride on the lake to the trekking site.  There are lovely trails here ranging  from very easy to moderate.  The moderate trail leads to a beautiful view of glaciers across a small valley. A little gem of a trail.  A few hours later the boat returns to the southern end of the lake and an opportunity to take a short but somewhat demanding hike to a turquoise glacier lake and Huemul glacier.  Overall a great day of moderate hiking with delightful endpoints.

However, the tour company needs to up its game in terms of customer service.  On the good side, the trip was punctual and comfortable.  However there was minimal engagement with the visitors.  The gentleman who appeared to be the leader was also the bus driver but he had little to say.  The group leader told the group that she didn't know much about the area and her job was to just organize the group and she wouldn't be saying anything along the bus ride.  And she was true to her word - she chatted with a friend about boyfriends.  I am not a traveler who thinks everyone in other countries should speak English, and my Spanish is fine, but I thought it was unusual in tourism that there was no English explaining the day since there were many foreign tourists for whom English is the lingua franca.  At the boat dock, there wasn't much explanation on any language and all the participants were wondering what they were supposed to do next.   At the trekking site, there were explanations in both Spanish and English and this was the first time that the day's schedule was finally explained.  When the boat returned to the bottom of the lake and the was an opportunity to hike to Huemul, there was little information on the exact time we had to be back to the bus and the operators were annoyed when a handful returned before the time we thought we were expected back but after the time the operators expected us back.

Overall, really a great day and easily worth the cost.  I wouldn't hesitate to recommend doing this trip, but don't expect the level of tour handling that is so much more typical in Argentina tourism.

Además, en un tramo de la excursión quedamos sin guía, y no habíamos recibido indicaciones adecuadas para acceder al glaciar Huemul.

Muy linda excursión. Guías atentos con el turista. Puntuales y gentiles. Super recomendable. Paisaje increíble.

Consulte en la agencia del chalten exploradores lago del desierto y la chica me indico que los jueves salian de punta sur del lago a las 10am dejandome en punta norte. Y el sabado recogian a la gente a las 11am de punta norte para volver al Chalten. Le comente que el domingo tenia el vuelo a Bs As, y me confirmo que los sabados era la vuelta, y si habia alguna situacion podia pedir a gendarmeria que llame por radio al bote. Volvi a consultar lo mismo en el barco para asegurarme y me confirmaron lo mismo.

El sabado a las 11am estaba esperando con 2 norte americanos, un italiano y un suizo que venian de villa o'higgins. Como eran las 11:30 y no llegaban, el suizo consulta por mensaje a la oficina del chalten, donde le indican que le diga a gendarmeria que ellos llamen por radio al bote si venian a recogernos. Del bote les responden a gendarmeria que vendrian al dia siguiente, el domingo. 

Al dia siguiente nos buscaron solo a nosotros. Cuando les consultamos porque no vinieron el dia que tenian programado, no nos dieron explicacion ni se disculparon.

Yo perdi el vuelo y tuve que comprar otro pasaje.

Reconozco lo bien que se porto la gente de gendarmeria que al ver la irregularidad de la situacion, nos consultaron si teniamos para comer a la noche, ofreciendonos pastas o necesitabamos algo.

Me parece que si es la unica agencia que hace un tour y cruce del lago, tendrian que respetar lo que prometen. Y no usar gendarmeria como guarderia de turistas o para comunicarse.

Muy buena experiencia. Los guías muy cordiales y serviciales.

Antes de salir hacia el sendero nos dieron varias indicaciones y una radio (porque íbamos solas por el sendero) con la cual uno de los guías se estuvo comunicando constantemente con nosotras para chequear que todo estuviera bien. Al llegar fue espectacular, lo valió completamente (así como todo en el Chalten). Luego, al regresar al domo, nos esperaron con un chocolate caliente y galletitas (estaba incluido en la excursión que compramos) como para completar la experiencia de mejor manera aún.

We rented a car in September 2024 and we made the Chico circuit and found this park . Free entry and a trail (very easy) to make (old , child ) . We take around 1 hour (travel) at the end of the trail has a lake and in the middle of the trail you find an arrayán tree forest (species of Patagonia). 
I suggest taking a paradinha on the site and walk the trail and see some of the vegetation of the site

Beautiful place: myrtle forest, forests, views of Llao Llao, Lago Escondido, viewpoints.
You can go from the center of Bariloche by bus: with bus 20 you have to get off at Puerto Pañuelo (the bus takes you behind the Civic Center on San Martin Street, where the artisans' tent is).
From Puerto Pañuelo you walk a few meters and you reach the beginning of the trail: the forest is very beautiful, there is a small forest of myrtle trees and further on you reach a beach on Lake Moreno from where you can see the Hotel Llao Llao, the viewpoint , the bridge over Lake Moreno that divides Moreno West and Moreno East, you can see trout, etc.
Continuing in the same direction you reach the route (Circuito Chico) and walking a few meters and crossing the route you can start another path to go to Lago Escondido, Bahia Los Trunks and Miradores del Capilla and Bahia Lopez.
We walked towards Bahia Lopez where the hotel is thinking about having a snack there, we only took a few snacks because unfortunately there weren't many options... The bus 10 passes by the hotel but has a very bad frequency (the next one was going to pass after 10 p.m.), so we walked towards the road to Colonia Switzerland. Buses 13 and 10 pass there. The 10 goes to the center of Bariloche but it was very full and we couldn't get on, so we took the 13 to km 18 and from there we combined with the 20 to return to the center of Bariloche.
If you can choose the day to go, I advise against going on Sundays since those are the days when there is a bus stop in Colonia Switzerland and the buses leave full from there and do not stop along the route.

My husband and I arrived by public transport to Puerto Pañuelo and then we walked to the access. At the entrance there is a place where you can buy something hot or drinks, it has several tables where you can have some mates and it has public bathrooms. During the breaks in our meeting, I gathered some information about places to visit. I, an Egyptian, and a Moroccan woman set out for Cerro Campanario. There, one can take a lifting chair up the mountain, providing a panoramic view of the entire Patagonian region. At the top, there’s a café where one can enjoy a light lunch. With the plan to have lunch and admire the mountain views, we boarded bus number 220 toward Cerro Campanario.
As the bus traveled through winding mountain roads, we passed dense forests, barren hills, and deep blue lake waters that captivated tourists. The bus stopped at various points, allowing passengers to get on and off. Based on my information, the driver would call out “Cerro Campanario,” and most passengers would disembark at that stop. However, after a long time, the driver didn’t make the announcement, and the majority of passengers remained on board. When I asked a fellow passenger, they mentioned that Cerro Campanario was still five stops ahead. Following their advice, we got off at the next stop to catch a bus going in the opposite direction.
Upon exiting the bus, we found ourselves in a dense forest with only a single, rarely traveled road. We couldn’t understand why there was a bus stop in the middle of such a secluded place. Standing inside a small tin shed, we waited for the bus while hoping there were no wild animals lurking nearby. Ten minutes later, the same bus returned, and the surprised driver looked at us and asked about our situation in fluent English. He then reassured us that he would personally drop us off at Cerro Campanario.
Once we got off the bus, we bought tickets for the chairlift up the mountain. Lately, I have been moving cautiously—though I won’t say why—so I hurried ahead and got on a chair alone. My two companions took the next chair. As the chairs ascended via cables, we gradually gained a breathtaking view of nature’s wonders. After a long ride, my chair finally reached the landing position.
A man at the top aimed his camera at me and said, “I’m taking your picture—look at me.” When I got off, another man showed me my picture on a tablet and said, “See how beautiful your photo turned out? If you want to receive it, pay three dollars at that counter and email us.” What a clever business model! But the photo was indeed stunning, so I paid three dollars, sent them an email, and received my picture.
At the mountain peak, there was a café with a rooftop view where everyone admired the beauty of the Andes. Hundreds of mountain peaks and the deep blue waters of the lake below created an enchanting scene. Breathing in the 100% pure air, I filled my lungs with freshness. Meanwhile, my stomach was making loud demands. We ordered an entire Patagonian beef pizza, which was too much for the three of us. We didn’t want to waste half of it, but we also felt hesitant to offer it to someone. Just then, two other participants from our meeting arrived. When we offered them the remaining pizza, they gladly accepted.
We spent a long time wandering around and taking pictures before descending via the chairlift before sunset. The next morning, at 8 AM, we bid farewell to Bariloche and flew to Buenos Aires.

We had to spend the night in the only "hotel" there, which offers terrible and expensive service (even for those with tents, the spot is more expensive than in some campsites in torres d'el Paine!), knowing that travellers have no other option. We went back to El Chalten the next morning. We had to pay back the catamaran on lake Desierto and the bus back to El Chalten...expenses that the agency refused to reimburse! 
We also learned later that the price for the boat on lake O'Higgins with this agency (80 USD) is much higher than the price paid directly on the boat or through another agency of El Chalten (56 USD).
The people who provide this service do know about service vocation, we spared a few hours with them and we felt that we were old friends. Thank you so much!!

A fuir absolument 
Il ne sert à rien de passer par cette agence pour faire la traversée jusqu'à Villa O'Higgins, mieux vaut se débrouiller par soi-même ou avec une autre agence. Mauvais service et aucun sens commercial. Leur seule valeur ajoutée aurait été de nous indiquer la veille de notre départ d'El Chalten - quand nous sommes allés leur demander - que le bateau en provenance de Villa O'Higgins pour faire la traversée depuis Candelario Mancilla le lendemain avait été annulé. Ils ne l'ont pas fait, et n'ont pas appelé la compagnie responsable du bateau à Villa O Higgins pour vérifier, alors que l'agence chilienne savait deja à cette heure là que le bateau ne partirait pas. Résultat nous avons du prendre un bus, un bateau sur le lac Desierto, marcher 22km en se dépêchant car nous avions découvert à la douane argentine que le bateau pour Villa O Higgins passait généralement beaucoup plus tôt qu'indiqué par l'agence (!), pour apprendre à l'arrivée que le bateau ne passerait pas. Nous avons du dormir sur place dans un endroit miteux à un prix exorbitant (même pour ceux qui ont une tente), et sommes repartis le lendemain pour El Chalten en devant repayer le catamaran sur le lac Desierto et le bus de retour à l'agence. Mais, alors même que leur incompétence nous a coûté une somme considérable d'argent et de temps qui aurait pu être évitée par un simple coup de fil de leur part avant notre départ, l'agence a refusé de nous rembourser le trajet de catamaran et de bus retour ! A noter en plus que nous avons appris plus tard que l'agence vend le trajet en bateau Candelario Mancilla - Villa O Higgins à un prix beaucoup plus cher (80 USD) que le prix vendu sur place ou via une autre agence d'El Chalten (les autres voyageurs passés par cette agence avaient payés 56 USD).

Fuimos hasta el embarcadero con nuestro vehículo para hacer la navegacion con Exploradores, todo el.personal muy amable, la chica de la boleteria, los asistentes del Canoero y la chica brasilera nos recibió en el domo ,nos explicó correctamente los senderos, al regresar nos esperó con refrigerio. Muy bien todo.
La verdad el tour no fué muy bueno por parte de la agencia, muy mala atención de la señorita Lucia. Poca predisposición. El chofer muy buena onda en todo el viaje

BUENO LES CONTAMOS LA EXPERIENCIA,SALIMOS A LAS 12 CON la combi. (eramos solo 6 pasajeros) el chofer lo unico que hacia era hablar con una chica colombiana, que parece trabajaba pro la zona. al llegar al puerto nos dijo que nos esperaba 18.20 hs- Al llegar a la embarcación para empezar la travesía faltaban dos señoras de Rosario,por ese motivos partimos 14.30. llegamos para empezar el treking, y nos recibió Juan, que nos dio el detalle de los caminos, y el horario de partida, asi que todos corremos para hacer el paseo de los senderos.Al volver al embarcadero no había nadie para recibirnos, así que los 4 nos dirijamos al glaciar huemul, bajando a las 18.30. Grande es nuestra sorpresa cuando el encargado del lugar donde te vendía las entradas no dijo que hace 10min  se había ido la combi con  solo 2 señoras, faltando los 4 pasajero)...nos desesperamos. la gente de ahi nos queria ayudar, pero sin señal de internet fue todo dificil.... a los 40 minutos .por suerte aparecieron autos y nos hicieron el favor de llevarnos al Chalten

Hemos pasado un hermoso día visitando los glaciares Vespignani y Huemul gracias a todo el equipo de Exploradores del Lago del Desierto.
Recomendamos esta experiencia en la naturaleza que no olvidarán nunca !!!

Hice la excursión Desierto Full con mis padres, que ya son personas mayores y los tres pudimos disfrutar de la excursión! Fuimos en el bus de las 12, asique nos acercamos a la oficina, desde donde salía el transfer. Luego de 1.30h de viaje llegamos al Lago. Desde allí tomamos la embarcación que nos dejo en la reserva del glaciar. Hicimos los senderos y luego nos volvimos a embarcar para ir hasta Punta Norte. Estuvimos una media hora mas o menos y luego regresamos. 
Todos fueron muy amables tanto en el puerto como las chicas de la oficina que tuvieron toda la paciencia para explicarles a mis padres de que iba cada excursión. 
Lo recomiendo muchisimo! Un paseo inolvidable!

He hecho la excursion Disierto Full. Super servicio.
Te conducen en un combi de buena onda a donde puedes compartir mate con el conductor hasta Punta Sur para navegar 15 minutos a donde te explican como las cosas se van a estar orgqanisadas y puedes salir el el fuente del pequeño bote para admirar el Fitz Roy y los glaciares al rededor y esteee aguaaa del lago del disierto. Que preciosa ! La vegetacion es realmente diferente. Despues de 15 minutos, llegas hasta el lugar de los pequenos trekking. Tienes bastante tiempo que para hacer los 3 caminatas o si tomas tu tiempo al los ñiradores, tienies bastante tiempo que al menos hacer 2 caminatas. Te consejo la roja. Hermosa ! Vas a caminar por tu cuenta pero hay guias en el lugar al domo que contestan a todas tus preguntas. Al regreso, tinies algunas gallitas, choco caliente y cafe para compartir con los guias y los otros turistos. Una ambiente familia en serio. 
Pero el mejor para la fin. Despues, fuimos hasta el punto norte del lago. Waw, mo hay palabras para describir la vista que tienes sobre de la cara norte del Fitz Roy. Hay que ir un dia sin nubes pero aparte de eso, incredible. El punto norte te trae tambien no se en una otra mundo. Yo me sienti como en un otro siglo, lo de la discubierta del Fitz. 
Despues por el regreso, el mismo.Por la excursion de la tarde, la suerte es que por el regreso te toca el atardecer poco a poco asobre de los glaciares y montañas. 
Te lo recomando sin dudos.Vale la pena poraue no es El chalten, un otro mundo. 
Sandy, de Belgica

I would strongly suggest to not work with this company. Firstly because its cheaper to do it yourself, secondly because its easy and finally because this company will treat you like garbage. 
We had booked transport to punta sur, the boat to cross the lake and 5 days later a boat to sail to O'Higgins from Mancilla. We planned to do a five day hike in between which was supposed to be the real highlight of our trip. 
The trouble began immediatly when we werent picked up in the morning, the company didnt answer their phone so we had to go to their office to find out they had forgotten us. At first they looked willing to solve our problem. They refunded a part of our money and arranged transport to punta sur. Since a couple of hours had past we would be to late to catch the boat so we would have to walk from south too north. Since we had to arrive at mancilla at the same day they PROMISED us a car would pick us up at 1830 at the border. After more then seven hours walking through the rain we arrived at the border at 1800, we waited for 2 hours but no car came. We had to set up camp on the spot and we were forced to cancel our multiday hike. The next day we walked to Mancilla and took the first boat to O'Higgins(wich we had to pay for ourselves since our ticket was for a few days later). When we arrived at O'Higgins I immediatly emailed the company to explain what had happened and that I wanted a full refund since they hadnt provided any services. Obviously I never received a response. I then proceeded to call them. At first they pretended they didnt know what I was talking about, a phone call later they didnt speak English anymore and the third call they pretended the reception was week. When I finally got contact via whatsapp (they spoke English again) they promised me a full refund and to keep me up to date on the process. That was the last I ever heard of them, they started completely ignoring my texts when I asked for an update after 10(10!!) days.
Short trail, ideal to combine with condor viewpoint and jump splash in the same day for those people who go with just the right days and do not want to miss anything

Although the entrance to the park is expensive (AR$45,000 ~ US$36/person), there are 2 good trails to do in about 3 hours.
The Mirador de Los Condores trail, which is shorter but steeper, and the Mirador das Aguilas trail, which is a bit longer but without difficulties, have a good, practically flat stretch. You can do both trails in a row, and the one I liked the most was the Aguilas trail. On the viewpoint you can see the large lake Viedma. The view is very beautiful and worth it.

This is the other viewpoints trail when you're going up towards the mirador de los condores hike just outside of town. Decent hike, not very strenous, it is way less crowded than the condores hike. At the viewpoint, you get views of the lake and glacier - we were lucky to see broken fragments of floating glaciers - its a good picnic spot if you wanted to enjoy a serene viewpoint while having sandwiches.

Esta caminata es de dificultad baja, hay un tramo en el que el guia avisa de un punto de no retorno, si se encuentran con molestias deben volver, en la cima se ve la ciudad del Chalten y el Fitz Roy.
En total no es mas de 1:30 entre subida y bajada, si quieren llevar un palo de trekking puede servirles, en mi caso me ayudó en una de las subidas, debido a una rodilla lastimada.

Lo hicimos en el dia de llegada, despues de Mirador de los condores. Tiene dificultad muy baja, y no lleva mucho tiempo. Llegando tenes hermosa vista del lago Viedma. Volviendo hicimos recorrido por arriba. Espectacular! Las vistas de altura son increíbles! Recomiendo hacer 2 senderos juntos. Tienen vistas distintas a El Chalten, Fitz Roy y lago Viedma. Imperdible recorrido!

Iniciamos el ascenso al mirador de Condores, pero antes de bajar, y con reserva de energia comenzamos  esta otra travesia que nos sorprendio al final con esa vista amplia hacia el oeste con la inmensidad del Lago Viedma, disfrutando alli de un buen tiempo para recuperarse y dejarse perder en la mirada.
Hay que hacer los 2 senderos.
Facil de llegar . Se hace en poco tiempo y Tiene una hermosa vista .   Ideal para  hacer cuando uno llega a la ciudad despues del mediodia .
Lo realizamos al otro día de haber nevado. Todo el paisaje era blanco. Se tiene una vista panorámica del lago Viedma. Hermosos paisajes!!

Son aprox 2 km de ida, de fácil acceso estando en el pueblo.
Linda vista del Chalten y el Fitz Roy. 
Para tomar unos mates si el tiempo lo permite.

Otro treking para la familia y de fácil acceso sin dificultades.  Solo 2 km x tramo.
Hermosas vista de todo los alrededores del chalten
Lejos la mejor vista del pueblo, caminas un poco más que el mirador del Cóndor pero es mucho más lindo!

Caminata liviana que se puede realizar con chicos y hasta con bebés. Si es con bebés, es indispensable llevarlo con mochila portabebé. Vistas hermosas de la ciudad y hermosos paisajes. Pasar por la oficina de información.

Apenas saliendo de la ciudad, al lado del Centro de Visitantes de la Administración de Parques Nacionales, inicia el sendero al mirador de los Cóndores y Las Águilas (una bifurcación). Tiene un desnivel suave, por lo que se hace accesible para casi todas las personas. El camino está bien señalizado y no reviste dificultad. Al llegar nos encontramos con una vista es impresionante. Se podrá ver un vasto escenario de estepa patagónica y a lo lejos  una vista panorámica sobre la estepa y el lago Viedma hacia el sur. También se alcanzan a ver los cerros Huemul y Pirámide.

A trilha até o Mirador Las Águilas começa na bifurcação sinalizada cerca de dez minutos antes de chegar ao mirante Los Condores. Para acessá-la, basta seguir o sinal indicativo da placa à direita e seguir em frente numa trilha de terra praticamente plana, com uma enorme montanha à direita.

Essa trilha curta tem um declive suave à medida que avança descobre o grande Lago Viedma no horizonte, mas nada complicado ou exigente.

O mirante fica à esquerda e tem uma vista panorâmica incrível para a estepe e o Lago Viedma a sul, o Monte Huemul a oeste e o Monte Pirámide a leste. Um lugar que merece ser aproveitado com muita calma.

Vale lembrar que essa trilha somente deve ser feita se o tempo estiver bom, pois se chover, a trilha ficará bastante perigosa e a visão do topo ficará muito prejudicada.

Detalhes: Distância total percorrida desde o escritório do Parque Nacional na base da montanha (ida e volta): 6 km 
Tempo: aprox. 3 horas no total.
Dificuldade: fácil
Subida Total / Descida: aproximadamente 200 metros

El sendero de este parque comienza a unos 1,8 km de la parada del colectivo N° 20 en puerto pañuelos caminando sobre la ruta como quien sigue circuito chico. 

Es un sendero de trekking de 2,8 kms a playa tacul (Divino lugar!! y el sendero es hermoso para hacerlo en familia, muy facil de hacer), en el camino de este sendero tienen la difurcacion al ascenso del cerro Llao Llao, no fui pero dicen que la vista es super magica, pero ojo el ascenso es algo exigido. Recomiendo hacer este sendero a Playa Tacul, es hermoso. Dia lluvioso o de viento NO LO HAGAN, es peligroso. En mi caso a la vuelta nos volvimos por la ruta por las dudas que nos lloviera!! 

DISFRUTEN!!! Y HAGAN TODO EN COLE DE LINEA INTERNAN QUE AHORRAN UN MONTON DE DINERO Y LOS LLEVA A TODOS LADOS!!

Hay varios lugares para recorrer en esta zona. El sendero y mirador tacul precioso. Villa tacul hermosa playa. Son caminatas en gral simples pero dentro del bosque. Muy lindo. Para varios días. Lago Moreno una playa más difícil para meterse al lago pero que bordeando el lago se tiene una vista hermosa del llao llao. Infinito bariloche.

Es un hermoso cerro para hacer trekking. Yo subí desde villa Traful. Es bastante duro para quieren no estamos acostumbrados a este tipo de actividad. Pero no es imposible y vale mucho la pena hacer el esfuerzo. La cima tiene una vista totalmente increíble. 
Camino muy empinado
Duración entre 40min a 1hs
Un trekking de un kilometro y medio a traves de un bosque con arrayanes y cohiues hasta el lago Moreno
La propaganda diría, véala, antes que desaparezca, que es lo que dicen que irá a suceder en pocos años.

Hicimos la caminata del sendero de Los Arrayanes. Super recomendable! Un bosquecito de Arrayanes divino! 
Realmente visitar este lugar es algo que recomiendo totalmente. No te lo pierdas, podes llegar en colectivo local desde el centro de la ciudad (pagas con la SUBE)
realmente visitar este lugar es algo que recomiendo totalmente. El bosque es fabuloso. No te lo pierdas, podes llegar en colectivo local desde el centro de la ciudad (pagas con la SUBE)

Pensando que en estas vacaciones las hago solo, debo tener presente que las cosas que haga me debo sentir a gusto, por lo que este lugar es imperdible, salvo la gente que justo te toca en la caminata, hablan fuerte, música en sus celulares, etc, falta de empatia y respeto a la naturaleza o a los demás que buscamos tranquilidad. Asique si yo lo pasé bien, con amigos o familia mejor, equipo de mate infaltable. Sin costo.

Hicimos la caminata del sendero de Los Arrayanes. Super recomendable! Un bosquecito de Arrayanes divino! Llegando a la playa, vistas muy lindas al hotel Llao Llao. Si caminas por la costa hacia la derecha, encontramos una parte del lago congelado, lo cual nos sorprendió y nos quedamos jugando un rato ( con niño de 9). Lindisimo para caminar por la costa con vistas geniales.

Hermoso, hay varios senderos para hacer y recorrer por este parque, bien señalizados y mantenidos.
Fuimos al mirador del cerro Llao Llao, nos encantó el camino, las vistas y sobre todo el final. A latarde volvimos de comer e hicimos el sendero del bosquecito de arrayanes y lago López, hermoso también aunque había mucha más gente.
Es un lugar excelente para pasear por los bosques y disfrutra del paisaje.
We have to keep pollution out of this beautiful place. So far, the efforts are non existent. But we all can get there. You can get here on public transport.

Es tan bonito !

Uno de mis lugares favoritos Villa Tacul, se respira mucha paz.
Playa. Viento. Arrayanes y senderos en el bosque.

Vale la pena conocerlo. Esta cerca del Puerto Pañuelo. En la entrada hay oficina de información, estacionamiento gratuito y baños públicos. Se puede tomar colectivo 20 en el centro de Bariloche o en cualquier parte de av. Bustillo. Pasa cada media hora. Bajar en el Puerto Pañuelo y seguir por la ruta 1km más o menos. Hay varios senderos de distinta dificultad. Desde oficina sale uno que va a la playa de lago Moreno, pasando un lindo mini bosque de arrayanes. Algunos senderos están conectados entre si, y otros tienen entradas por  la ruta. Más lindo para mi es Cerro Llao Llao, vale la pena subir. Es de dificultad media.Tiene vista increíble! Excelente lugar para relajarse y contemplar este hermoso paisaje. Hay que llevar agua y comida liviana para picnic. Poner zapatillas para tekking y ropa liviana. Los senderos están señalizados, pero hay que prestar atención.
Muy buena opción conectarse con la naturaleza cerca de Bariloche!

Fuimos por historia familiar. No lo conocía pero nos envolvió un silencio bellísimo, sólo pájaros se escuchaban. Un paseo no muy conocido pero hermoso. Por favor si van sean cuidadosos, no arrojen cosas y mucho menos fumar.

Es un parque municipal que vale la pena conocer. De Puerto Pañuelo, es mas o menos 1 km sobre la ruta a mano izquierda. Luego, dentro del lugar, en el ingreso hay una oficina de información, unos bancos para hacer pic nic y baños. 
Recomiendo hacerlo, ya que hay varios senderos de dificultad baja- media, con muy buenas vistas. 
Hay que tener en cuenta que en el sitio no hay para comer, ni agua por lo que hay que llevarse todo.

Es un recorrido hermoso y sencillo, vas a encontrar un pequeño bosque de arrayanes que vale la pena entrar!!

Luego podes seguir caminando por un paisaje hermoso de cañas hasta llegar a una pequeña playita, y si prestas atención podes encontrar bajadas al lago escondidas que valen la pena!

No esta muy bien señalizado asi que hay que tener cuidado, por ejemplo hay un cartel que te lleva al Lago Escondido y no recomiendo hacerlo desde acá porque el camino vuelve a sacarte a la ruta para llegar allí. Es mejor que vuelvas donde dejaste estacionado el auto y si aun quieres ir al lago escondido, puedes ir en auto y hacer una pequeña caminata por otro sendero.
Comimos una rica merienda con una vista increible, imperdible para un día de relax. Lindo para ir en pareja!

Un imperdible del circuito chico, hay lugar para estacionar y caminar, el recorrido dura aprox 2 hs entre ida y vuelta, se pueden ver el llao llamo de fondo y se llega hasta el lago encantado, la perlita es un bosquecito de arrayanes en el medio del parque!!!

LInda lugar para hacer trekking, recorrer los bosques del Llao y Llao y admirar el paisaje. Recomiendo este circuito para hacer con niños pequeños que no estén acostumbrados a caminar mucho o para personas mayores ya que hay varios niveles de dificultad y bastantes lugares para parar a retomar energías-

Llao llao patagonia, argentina is one of the most remarkable places in the western hemisphere. Beautiful beyond description and yet very accessible. I have visited 5 times and still looking forward to my next trip.

It is a scam, if you find an arrayan I congratulate you, nothing to do with the photos that show you to sell the tour, but you want to feel scammed do not go, and if you want to take the desire you can enter x villa the free angostura.

It is not at all what you see in the photos, on the catwalk circuit I will have seen 10 arrayans hopefully. They're almost gone. If you do the full trail you see many more and it is more entertaining. It is not worth paying for a boat + admission fee to go to that alone. For that it is better to go bariloche to the path of the arrayanes of the llao llao that is free.
In short, if you do the full trail it is entertaining to walk, it is quite demanding but it is very well marked and without any obstacles. If you go by boat alone to the forest you will be disappointed

If you are in Bariloche or Villa la Angostura, you cannot miss the excursion to the Arrayanes Forest.  
It lasts approximately 3 hours, of which 45 minutes are on the ferry. 
The entire landscape is beautiful, the guide's explanations are very interesting and complete, and the energy of the place is unmatched.

A must-see excursion in San Carlos de Bariloche, it integrates the tour with Isla Victoria and lasts almost a day while there is light.
       Very nice tour, without major difficulty, it is necessary to hire it with a company because it is a protected area, it departs by catamaran from Puerto Pañuelo and it is a nice refreshment for the senses and to admire a landscape of enormous beauty in Argentina.

We visited this site with a Turisur excursion combined with Victoria Island. The catamaran first visited the Arrayanes Forest. The visit consists of walking about 700 meters along a wooden walkway seeing these wonderful trees of different shapes and that characteristic color. We had a fairly cold day with sleet at times, but on this section of the walk it didn't rain and we were able to enjoy it. I must say that 14 years ago I took this same walk and the trees had a more intense, more vivid color. Now they look a little more opaque and lackluster. In any case, it is a highly recommended walk, not only through the forest but also because of the catamaran ride, which is also very nice.

Beautiful place, with planks and steps. Option of alternative ramp and 'smooth' area to go with a wheelchair, although WITH HELP since it is not easy, there is mud and significant inclinations, but 'it can be done'. We went with the company CAU CAU which was EXCELLENT.

El bosque esta muy deteriorado, muchos ejemplares secos y otro tanto descoloridos, segun nos indicaron (cuando ya estabamos alli) el cambio climatico los esta afectando, por supuesto que esto no es responsabilidad de las personas que hacen los tours, pero te venden unas fotos que no son actuales y terminas pagando un monton de dinero para ver troncos secos, ademas, las pasarelas estan en mal estado y ni que hablar del muelle, tablas podridas, otras sueltas, un desastre. La cabaña del bosque, la promocionan como casa de te, pero resulta que por dentro es una mugre y te encuentras con un expendio de te y cafe en vasos de telgopor, con una o dos tortas espantosas para elegir, un par de sandwich envueltos en film, una heladera con jugos de cajita y latitas, mas parecido a un kiosco de mal gusto.

Hermoso lugar. Debo decir que lo padecí pero por no tener experiencia en el calculo de distancia jajaj. ingrese a caminar sin nada mas que ver que onda. Me costo 3hs ida y 3hs vuelta terminas arruinado sino estas en buen estado. En alguno casos tienen pendientes de 45° son mortales. pero el paisaje es hermoso. ahhh se puede descansar y seguir hay muchos lugar para tomar buenos mates y seguir la caminata
No vale la pena, no es una excursión interesante en ningún sentido. Es carísima y la casita de te está descuidada y no tiene nada para merendar
Espantoso. Casi no quedan arrayanes. La pasarela toda rota. Una vergüenza que comercialicen el parque en ese estado. Lleno de gente, todo descuidado

Realizamos la visita tras una larga caminata desde el ingreso del parque (aproximadamente 3 horas). El recorrido por las pasarelas es en un circuito circular y permite admirar estos árboles tan particulares. En lo personal,disfrutamos más del trayecto hasta el bosque que de la visita al mismo en sí, tal vez por la gran cantidad de visitantes en ese momento. El acceso a la confitería es complicado, ya que es la única opción para el gran número de visitantes que el bosque recibe. Los baños estaban en condiciones aceptables.
Desastre en el bosque. Descuidado. Los arrayanes sin color. Nadie que de una explicación. Tristeza. Feo volver y ver el bosque así.

Lo unico bueno es el viaje en catamaran pero para eso hay mil opciones aca en villa y en todo el sur.
El bosque de arrayanes ya casi no tiene arrayanes... la pasarela espantosa q hicieron hace 30 años esta toda rota y para caminar el bosque hay montones de senderos mas naturales y lindos. NO la hagan

Horrible. El bosque esta muy descuidado, los arrayanes casi inexistentes, tapado por otra vegetacion y casi muertos o descoloridos. La pasarela en mal estado. La playa sucia y descuidada tambien. En años anteriores el paseo era un lugar hermoso pero en la actualidad se encuentra en un estado deplorable.

El bosque es lindo y es algo distinto, pero no es Wow, es un bosque.
No la recomiendo como excursión principal, hay mejores cosas que ver antes como los 7 lagos por ejemplo.
El paseo por el bosque dura unos 25/30 minutos.
Al dia de hoy la casa de Te y los baños estaban cerrados
El catamaran que te lleva cuesta $1800/2000  , tenes una hora de ida una hora en el bosque y una hora de regreso.
Recomiendo llevar comida par almorzar.
Solo aceptan efectivo en los puestos de venta
La entrada al parque cuesta $230 si sos Argentino.

Faz parte de um passeio conjugado com a Isla Victoria, feito por duas empresas ótimas (turisur e cau-cau). O acesso por barco em um pier de fácil acesso e o passeio é basicamente uma volta por uma trilha de escadarias de madeira, fáceis de andar e subir. Para quem tem dificuldade de locomoção vai ser mais difícil. Cadeiras de rodas não indicaria. As crianças gostam bastante do passeio. Levem água e algo para comer, tanto no barco quanto nos dois locais.

Passeio para quem curte natureza. Foi uma das paradas do passeio da Cau Cau. O passeio de barco é a grande atracao. A parada em Isla Victoria e Bosque arrayanes sao os coadjuvantes. É bonito, mas ok. Nada demais.
Então... primeiro você faz o circuito chico, e vê as árvores e as cores da estação mais especial - o outono - e, depois, voçê caminha entre essas cores e árvores. Pra mim, fantástico. Vou repetir!

Lindo paseo al bosque pero que dejaria como relleno de tener dias de sobra, tanto por el costo al ir en catamaran como por lo que es. Hice la excursión Lago del Desierto Full y me pareció increíble. El viaje hacia punta sur del lago del desierto es increible, la flora y fauna de todo el camino nos dejaron impactados y enamorados de sus bosques.

Try to avoid the times when the large tour buses arrive. Here is what we experienced on a Sunday in January (we drove in a rental car):

9.45am - the entire parking lot was full of tour buses, huge line. We decided to do other things on the circuito chico and come back later. 

2.50pm (1450hrs) - no line, found parking at the end of the lot. Within minutes a large tour bus arrived so we quickly bought our tickets and went up.

3.40pm (1540hrs) - when we came back down we found 8 tour buses in the parking lot and a long line waiting. This must have been the afternoon round of half-day tours.

Wanted to share dangerous experience I had today at the chairlift.

It was really a traumatic experience today  riding for 20 min in the open chairlift without a security bar closed. 
Beyond this traumatic and really  dangerous experience, I was shocked by the attitude of the Cierro Campanario staff immediately after that incident, the guide saying "just forget about it" and the Bariloche city tourist office that told me just complete complaint form and was very relaxed telling me it never happened before.
I came with a tour group and was sitted in the chairlift cabin. The security bar didn't close and went back up. I yelled to the staff nearby please stop it and close the bar, I'm in totally open cabin but they did nothing and in 1 sec I was high above the ground. It was 20 min of nightmare to go up the mountain, tilting in the air and trying to hold the side bars as strong asap. I was terrified and still have chest pains. 
I'm afraid of heights in general and this experience was really terrible. 
When I arrived to the upper stop the staff jumped to take my pic to sell it to me later and when I yelled and showed that I was all the way without a security bar they laughed.
I told the group guide about it and his response was "just forget about it".
This incident destroyed my tour and my whole trip. I still have 3 weeks in Argentina and Chile before coming back home to Israel and I'm just devastated.

It's life threatening situation that should be treated very seriously by the authorities and not allow this reckless operations.

If you're ever in Bariloche, visiting Cerro Campanario is an absolute must! As soon as I reached the summit, I was greeted with the most awe-inspiring panoramic views I have ever witnessed. The entire ride up on the chairlift is serene and peaceful, offering a taste of the spectacular scenery you’re about to experience at the top. Once there, you can see it all—Lago Nahuel Huapi stretching endlessly, the forests, and the rugged mountains in the distance. It’s like stepping into a postcard.

Whether you're an avid photographer or someone just seeking tranquility, Cerro Campanario will not disappoint. Trust me when I say, you’ve got to see it to believe it. I'll be back for sure to experience this slice of paradise again.

It is a tour with a very beautiful view and it is possible to do on your own. 
Take the bus in the city center and get off the door, the rates to get up are the same by agency. I recommend!

Climbing the Cerro Campanario on a clear day is to be able to appreciate all the exuberance of nature. The region of the lakes has this name is not the shade, the Cerro is surrounded by numerous lakes that provide breathtaking views. It's fantastic!
It is worth taking the cable car and seeing a stunning view of the city. I recommend eating meat empanada and a wine, with a beautiful view of the mountains with ice at the peak.

The Chico Circuit is the most emblematic scenic route in Patagonia, a journey of about 60 km bordering lakes and mountains. On this walk you will visit Cerro Campanario to enjoy one of the best views in the world, the historic Hotel Llao Llao, the picturesque Chapel San Eduardo, the must-see Panoramic Point and finish in Cologne Switzerland. It is almost obligatory to do so because it allows to capture the true essence of Bariloche in just half a day (or full day if you stop for lunch and snack), combining unspoilt nature, Alpine architecture and dreamy viewpoints. You can’t leave the city without walking its curves and stopping at every corner to take the classic Argentine postcard.

It is the panoramic walk that takes you to the main points of the city, with fascinating views of Cerro Campanario, with its panoramic viewpoint, Hotel Llao Llao and its surroundings, and Villa Tacul, on Lake Nahuel Huapi. Also of interest are the Chapel San Eduardo, the Panoramic Point, the Arroyo Angostura and the Patagonia Brewery.

Then we went to lunch at the Patio Brewery, you find variety of options.
All walk 100% Recommended.

El lugar cuenta con varios lugares donde estacionar el auto y recorrer luego a pie alguno de sus senderos que no presentan excesiva dificultad. También durante el circuito iremos encontrando diversos miradores, alguno a pie de carretera.

Me refiero a la que se tiene desde la cumbre del cerrito llao llao.
Anteriormente estuve recorriendo los otros senderos del parque municipal y me faltaba hacer este sendero al cerro llao llao.
El sendero es algo largo y relativamente fácil,solo al final y algunos tramos por la erosión es algo mas dificultoso ya que presenta tierra suelta,raíces y sanjones.
No esta señalizado asi que hay que prestar atencion de seguir por el sendero principal.La vista es muy linda,no es a los 360 grados pero se aprecia hacia una zona ,al norte del lago todo el paisaje con amplitud.
Realizarlo insume unas 3-4 horas entre ida y vuelta desde el inicio del sendero en  la ruta del circuito chico a unos 500 metros después del centro de informes.
Natureza exuberante, ótimo para fazer caminhadas, relaxar e contemplar a belíssima natureza Patagônica.

Dentro del Parque LLao LLao hay una zona del que salen senderos,  específicamente el lugar es un estacionamiento que esta identificado en el mapa que brinda la Sec. De Turismo.
Hay un sendero corto y sin mucha dificultad, de unos 40 minutos em el que se pueden ver arrayanes. Están señalizados y cuidados.
Una buena opción de caminata gratuita.

Bonito paseo, por lo menos la primera parte, con el minibosque de arrayanes. Pero el sendeno no tiene señalización interna, nunca sabés dónde estás ni cuánto falta para llegar a quien sabe dónde. Eso es común en todos los circuitos de Bariloche. Si por mí fuera ya habría despedido por inútil al responsable de turismo de la provincia.

Parte do circuito Chico. O que eu mais amei foi a trilha (sendero) ao cerro LLAO LLAO. Do topo, uma das vistas mais lindas que já tive o privilégio de ver. Depois do topo, descemos e fomos à praia na villa Tacul.

Este verano 2020 volví a hacer el ascenso al Cerro LLAO LLAO. Es un sendero de baja dificultad y se llega a una cima rocosa que tiene una de las mejores vistas!
Si vas en auto, lo podés dejar en el estacionamiento del parque municipal. Aprovechàs el baño público que està medianamente en condiciones. Pedís un plano en la oficina de información, si tenés la suerte de que esté abierta. Tiene a la vista los horarios de atenciòn pero no se respetan. 
Si estàs a pie como yo. Tomàs el colectivo 20 de la empresa Mi bus. Y te bajàs en la penúltima parada, Puerto Pañuelo.Seguís por la calle unos 300metros y te encontràs con la entrada al Parque Municipal. No entràs. Seguís y a mano derecha aparece la indicaciòn del sendero hacia el Cerro Llao Llao y Villa Tacul.
El sendero es sombreado.Muy agradable de transitar. Sólo en los últimos tramos se vuelve empinado. Importante ir con calzado cómodo, una provisión de agua y una vianda ligera.
Nada màs lindo que comer una fruta o un sandwich contemplando semejante paisaje.
Es una de las màs lindas caminatas de medio día cercanas a la ciudad de Bariloche.
It is worth walking to the top of Llao Llao, the views are quite stunning. Moderate walk, easy to follow and accessible by bus.

Tiene estacionamiento gratuito y desde allí se pueden realizar algunas caminatas no muy largas. Hay un bosquesito de arrayanes y se puede llegar a la costa del lago y recorrerla bastante. Nos gusto. Baños en mal estado y sucios. No había personal para información como indicaban los carteles.
Las vistas son realmente increíbles. El Hotel Llao-llao es hermoso y está ubicado en una colina con una vista inmejorable.

You just don't want to go any further away! The view catches you, it is fascinating, splendid, it is not possible so much beauty!
Of course, the day has to be beautiful, no clouds, it's unforgettable!
Great place to enjoy the lake and the mountains of Bariloche. Entrance paid with sale on site and with good price. You can go with agency and/or own car or rental.
Really the viewpoints are fantastic, we arrived missing 5min to the closing and the staff did not fail to measure efforts to climb.

The site has good infrastructure, the staff are kind and the landscape is stunning.
In addition to the panoramic view that has a sensational view, the other viewers also bring us beautiful landscapes.

Actually, we didn't plan to go here, but our Guide who took us to the Chico Circuit told us it was one of the stops. The line for the cable car is a little long and slow, but the view from the top is ALL WORTH IT. The cable car guys are friendly and already up there you have a 360 view of all the nature in Bariloche, it really is beautiful. The restaurant did not eat anything, but it looks cozy and apart has a lovely kitten there asleep :3 Grab your belongings very well on the cable car climb. I dropped one of my gloves and obviously there was no way to recover it anymore:c Of the most beautiful and stunning views I saw in Bariloche definitely.

The panoramic view of the bell tower was considered by National Geoghapic as one of the 5 most beautiful in the world.

When I arrived at the place I noticed that it actually makes jus the fame.

The climb is by cable car, oq by itself is already a great experience.

On top there is a confectionery with great chocolate, coffee, sweets, souvenirs and souvenirs.

Very worth it, wonderful place.

Impermissible for those in Bariloche.
It is one of the most beautiful views of Bariloche. It's a compulsory stop at the Chico Circuit. You can also get there easily by car, taxi, remis or Uber. It's worth seeing.

Must see in Bariloche . The cost of the chairlift to be able to climb the mountain is $ 12,000 adults and less $ 7000, as in every bariliche you have to arrive early, we arrived at 8 45 in the morning and there were more than 50 people trained to buy ticket and start climbing. Only two or one person can climb in the chairlift. Above are views that there is no way to describe until you can see it. There are several points where you can take pictures of different mountains and lakes around Bariloche. There are several photographers who can get you better photographs that are worth $6000 pesos either digital or printed. We had a sunny morning so they were perfect photographs.
The view is beautiful, whether from the Andes mountains or the lakes. I went in the late afternoon it was very cold. Then go straight.

We go up the trail in semi snowy winter and it can get complicated, because the roads freeze and are very steep, however it is completely worth seeing the beautiful views offered by the top of the hill and having a coffee in the confectionery that is at the top of the place.

It was a beautiful place....but I don't know what happened to it, after 3 years of not going I found a decayed place, old, dirty, abandoned many closed businesses, and signs of not parking aggressive, all without an order and to finish they were making the main street!!!! Yesiii in January! Something inexplicable, chaos to walk and to park, I do not recommend it.

I went by line collective from Bariloche expecting to find some typical European village architecture and found none of that. It's all prepared for the "buy I bought, buy." I mean local handicrafts and food on the way. 'Cause the day I went, there wasn't even a lot of it. 
I discovered, by chance, that there is a public beach above the lake. And I say "by chance" because the entrance sign is not very visible

I don't recommend it, there's no parking a chaos downtown, the main street covered with dirt because they're putting cobblestone. We really lost the day I thought I found something related to the colony and there were the same crafts you find everywhere.  I hope they can improve it, today it is not in condition

The very picturesque place, ideal to take some photos and enjoy some mattes and nothing else. These are only handicraft fairs and food courts between nature and very well set, but with excessive prices, there is also no good cell phone signal and no wifi so there is no other than the cash payment. I arrived early and I could enjoy the quiet of the morning, then it was crowded, they cut off the traffic on the main street that they are asphalting and in the entrance street generated a bottleneck as it is a very small street. I went by public transport taking the 20 from the center of Bariloche to the roundabout of km 18 and then the collective 13. Collective 10 from the center goes straight but passes every two hours.   In the afternoon due to excessive traffic the groups divert without warning, we were a group of people waiting and the groups did not come in the schedule that they should pass until we were informed that they should divert so we shared a taxi to km 18 of Bustillo to take the 20. Another option is to travel by hand to the roundabout. It was Wednesday and they were curious but most of them are for sharing (I was alone), there was only one place I had individual but I thought too 30000 pesos for what it is. The best thing to visit on the spot the beach on Lake Perito Moreno, there is a descent meters from the entrance to the main street in front of the chapel.

A pity the disorganization... the lack of information and the mistreatment of some of the members of "teansito".
They're tarmac and they won't warn you...
The village is very small (and beautiful) so NO PLACES for parking. And the ones there are "private" (I don't know if the sidewalks can be) and expensive. 
No one tells you that there is a huge and highly recommended Craft Fair...
Not recommended, little investment, ! Land streets with a couple of locals ...transit and park chaos ...expensive for what is the place ...
Massy and expensive. Food with exorbitant prices (example burgers in food truck at $18000, equivalent to 18 euros).

There is a place, a supposed park, that has the "Fountain of Youth", "Enchanted Lagoon" and "Fountain of Wishes" where you have to pay a ticket supposedly at will but still the owner, Mario, puts a price on which he always earns the same amount of money. First we got there being four and he said it was 20,000 per person usually, then a couple came and told them it's usually given 50,000 per person. The place is neglected, they are two dirty lagoons where the trout hopefully survive and not worth it at all. It's not worth paying a weight.
Wide variety of places in which to buy crafts and souvenirs, variety of craft beers. Try a very good lamb sandwich!!!

Cologne Switzerland is very nice. It is easy to reach from Bariloche in 30 minutes. I recommend staying between 11 and 11:30, approaching the box and paying for the tray of curanto for two people ($25,000, includes different cuts of meat and several vegetables). In the main food court, which is outdoors, there are as many food options as pizza, tacos and empanadas. In the case of curanto, it is usually served between 13:45 and 14:00. At all times there are artists playing and/or singing folklore and tango on a stage. Peña wave, very nice. While you wait for lunch, you can tour the craft stalls that are several. For children there are games. There are also some restaurants. Only visit on Wednesdays or Sundays. I think it's Saturdays too. Don't go another day because there's no movement and you don't enjoy it.

Hermoso sendero por donde podes recorrer una pequeña parte del bosque. Lleno de arrayanes, para mi la especie más linda de villa la angostura, y lleno de muchísimas otras especies. Hay un camino para ir y volver desde el puerto de villa la angostura hasta este sendero que toma unas 3 a 4 horas por tramo. Unas 6 a 8 horas ida y vuelta . Sino se puede ir y volver en barco. El trayecto en el barco es súper hermoso. Se ve todo angostura por el agua. Al final de este sendero hay una casa de té que sirven unas tortas riquísima y súper abundantes, además de un rico chocolate o café. Lamentablemente esta parte del bosque está enferma, los arrayanes están enfermos y no se sabe porque aún. Es un punto obligado de la villa. Lo súper recomiendo.
Para quem quer passar um dia surpreendente pela beleza na natureza, este é o lugar. Vale a pena gastar uma tarde para este lugar mágico.

Es una excursión para estar en contacto con la naturaleza. El bosque de arrayanes está en la península de quetrihue a unos 40 min de navegación desde la isla Victoria por eso es una excursión que suele hacerse junta.
También puede accederse desde Villa la Angostura.
No hay mucho para hacer, es simplemente un sendero de 800 m dentro del parque Nahuel Huapi que te muestra un bosque repleto de este árbol tan característico, es una zona de preservación por eso hay que transitarla prudentemente. Hay baños disponibles y una cafetería donde se puede comprar chocolate caliente.
Cuenta la leyenda que este bosque inspiró a Walt Disney en la realización de la película Bamby.
Recomendaciones: los tramos de barco son largos, 2 de más de 1 hs y otro de 40 min. Se puede llevar mate y vianda y aprovechar para comer y tomar algo porque comprar es bastante caro.
Se puede recargar agua para el mate en el puerto y en barco.
Realmente es encantador pero todo el atractivo esta en la naturaleza
Extras: entrada al parque: $140 y tasa de embarque $63

La verdad es que si vas a La Angostura o Bariloche esta excursión la tenes que hacer. El lugar es de ensueño. Si te da la nafta, te recomiendo hacerlo en bicleta desde La Angostura, y si se te acaba la nafta volves en el barco.

Fuimos un día de llovizna con catamarán Patagonia,(podes pagar con mercadopago) pudimos almorzar dentro ya que tiene mesitas,las chicas excelentes,super atentas y dispuestas. El viaje de 45 min fue estupendo,mis hijos se prendieron a darle de comer restos de pancitos a las gaviotas. Al llegar la caminata por el bosque fue aún más hermoso,los arboles super verdes y adornados con las gotas de lluvia,el paseo fue muy lindo aún con el mal tiempo ya que debajo de los árboles no te mojas. la casita de te preciosa y el chocolate caliente riquísimo. El chico que nos atendió super amable.

Fuimos al bosque de arrayanes con la ilusión de encontrar un lugar típico de Te y nos encontramos en l famosa casita de bambi un Maxi quiosco de cuarta IMPRESENTABLE sirven el chocolate de una máquina en un vaso descartable que triste

É uma parte do passeio que vai para Isla Victoria. É um bosque realmente bem diferente pelos famosos Arrayanes e sua cor de canela. Ao contrário do que dizem, Walt Disney não se inspirou nele pra fazer o Bambi e nem esse personagem é um huemul típico da Patagônia. É um passeio simples, eu diria.
Lugar imponente... Transmite mucha paz... Un lugar lindo para disfrutar en familia... Vistas hermosas.. Muy recomendable
Podes llegar a traves de una caminata de 12km por el bosque, o en excursion con catamaran, es un lugar hermoso y armonioso para disfrutar y recorrer tranquilos.

Se puede llegar a pie o en barco contratando las excursiones en los locales que están antes de llegar a los muelles. Está la opción de ir y volver en barco, ir caminando hasta el bosque y volver en barco o al revés: ir en barco y volver caminando.
Yo me incline por ir por agua y volver por tierra pero creo que lo mejor es a la inversa. Son 12 km de caminata por entre la paz y vegetación del bosque, increíbles. Además de que es uno de los senderos de los que conforman "Huella andina". Una vez entre los arrayanes uno no puede creer lo lindos que son y lo frio que están. Cerquita del muelle del bosque hay una cafetería ideal para contrarrestar el frio de afuera si uno va en invierno.
Hermoso lugar, especial para sacar fotos. Muy linda experiencia en el Modesta Victoria. No se lo pierdan.

es la 3ra vez que voy y cada vez me resulta mas magica, siempre se descubren nuevas cosas, colores y vistas, unicos en el mundo es una experiencia para repetir mil veces.
Pequeño dato.... el viaje en barco desde bariloche sale $1100 y desde la angostura la mitad. si pueden,, salir de alla es mas barato, e incluso se puede elegir ir caminando x un sendero de 12 Km solo abonando el ingreso al parque (250 extranjeros, 125 argentinos, y 50 pesos residentes de nqn o rio negro)

El Paseo entre arrayanes por la península Quetrihué Es una experiencia única. Impecable pasarelas y el famoso café de Bambi. 
Altamente recomendable caminarla y disfrutar de sus colores y sus sonidos. Hermosa la laguna Patagua

El camino para llegar al bosque de Arrayanes son 12 km aproximadamente. Mucha gente va caminando, otros en barco que cuesta entre 400/650$ por persona (éste tarda 1 hora para ir, otra para volver, y otra para permanecer en el bosque). Nosotros fuimos en bici, es un trayecto con pendientes pronunciadas entonces tuvimos que bajar de la bici muchas veces, tardamos 1.30/2 hs en ir y otras tantas en volver. Al llegar al bosque, hay pasarelas para recorrerlo y un muelle con una vista increíble.

Fuimos desde Villa la Angostura ..ya que se aprovecha la visita a la cuidad ..y después se hace la isla con un costo la mitad más económico que saliendo desde Bariloche ..
El paseo es relativamente corto pero vale la pena los arrayanes son los protagonistas además de los ciprés y demás 
Se abona la entrada a parques nacionales y el pasaje del catamarán hasta la isla ...
Lo que recomiendo es llevar su bebidas ..aguas ,gaseosas para hidratarse..ya que en la isla hay un solo bar (cabaña)  los precios son excesivos ...

En si el bosque es interesante y lindo si te interesan los árboles. Pero no es nada demasiado llamativo. Lo que recomiendo es el sendero que va desde puerto Angostura hasta el bosque. Son 12 km que se vuelven muy divertidos si se realizan en mountain bikes. Esta bien señalizado pero hay que tener cuidado con los peatones que comparten sendero.

Excelente para hacer en bicicleta. Es largo, 12km de ida y de vuelta, es el mismo sendero. En muchos lugares tenes que bajarte y llevar la bici en el piso, aproximadamente en total son 3/4km con bici en la mano y el resto pedaleando, o casi sin pedalear por que hay muchas bajadas y subidas que subis con el envión. Muy seguro el camino. Hacerlo en bici es excelente, muy largo para hacerlo caminando, aprovecharía para hacer otros trekings caminando. Bici en el medio del bosque, con muy lindas vistas. El cansancio vale la pena! 4/5hs en total entre ida y vuelta y recorrido por el bosque (que esta al final de la isla).

Visita obligada para toda aquella persona que esté en villa la Angostura, le guste la actividad al aire libre y las vistas espectaculares
También recomiendo muchísimo hacer el trayecto con bicicleta, ir con comida (en el bosque está carísimo) y mucha agua. Si llegan muy cansados tienen la chance de volver en barco

Una caminata larga pero llena de naturaleza y flora. Se ven pocos Arrayanes de pie, la verdad es que actualmente están muchos caídos pero es una gran opción. Se puede hacer en bicicleta o caminando. Muy importante llevar mucho líquido, dado que solo se puede comprar una vez finalizado el recorrido en una casa de té a un precio elevado

Muy pintoresco lugar. Hermoso el circuito por la pasarela. Imposible perderse. Lástima que nos llevaron a las corridas y el fotógrafo muy pesado para sacarte una imagen en la casita (carísima La foto!!!!).
It's worth the visit as the cable car is working and maintained in good condition and at an acceptable price for the fun.

Excellent! He
Best destination in Bariloche for trekking or climbing. Full of unbeatable landscapes and beautiful places to sleep.

If they survive the provincial route (Vialidad de Río Negro) that is completely destroyed in its 40km to Pampa Linda, and even respecting the passing schedules that some brainless people do not comply with and no one is there to do a check, they will reach a Amazing place. The attention at the CAB campsite is bad. Not so in shelters, where attention stands out. The trails are poorly marked and without any maintenance, which makes them very risky for people who are not in excellent physical condition. In Pampa Linda the CAB should have someone to provide advice. With the rates charged in the shelters it should not impact the club's economy.

The landscape is beautiful, the imposing hill, the road is not very good, that's why the three stars, the last stretch is gravel 40 km, very tedious with saws and many stones, supposedly although there are traffic times in which the single lane must be respected because of the narrowness of the road this is not fulfilled, because of this and because of giving way to traffic that was circulating in the opposite direction, a stone cut our tire, my recommendation is to stay in Pampa Linda or Playas Negras, it is not worth going to Tronador
I was impressed by the beauty of the place! With the size of the hill, and seeing the black glacier. I recommend the experience.

Great place. Impressive walk. We went with the people from Turaccion. Excellent service from Maria and the driver, Marcelo. Advice. Avoid the Los Rapidos camping site. Prices without shame. Example? 500 pesos for a plastic spoon to be able to eat yogurt bought from them!! One of those white spoons, the ones they give you anywhere...except for this, excellent experience.

There are 48 km of gravel, from the entrance to the parking lot, the truth is that up to the tronador hotel it is in perfect condition, but the last 16 km is quite deteriorated. From the parking lot to the Snowdrift it is worse. It can be done by car, you don't need to have a 4x4 (it's more of a convenience). The views are incredible!
The place is beautiful, unique, worth visiting. Chance to hear the crash of a piece of ice breaking off the mountain

Magnificent mountain formation. It's a long way to get there and the road is very bad, narrow and full of potholes. Upon arrival the van was unable to climb, chains were required. Unfortunately it was raining a lot, but the view was incredible. The tour lasts all day and you have to pay to enter the national park.

O lugar é muito lindo e tem neve o ano todo. Mas muitas horas de estrada de terra para pouco se aproveitar do lugar. No inverno há apenas um restaurante e fica lotado, sem condições de atender toda a demanda. Não recomendo.

It is a spectacular place!!! Of the nicest places I've ever visited. It has on the way several very nice trails that go between the forests, viewpoints that take you around the lake with beautiful views and the panoramic point is a postcard! SUPER RECOMMENDED!
Amazing panorama! Breathtaking. Definitely one of the highlights of our trip! Don’t miss this place in Bariloche. Enjoy!
Rent a car and stop and go as you wish. More to do and more scenic than the Ruta de Siete Lagos drive. Some good restaurants to stop for lunch. Plan your hikes and beach stops.

Gorgeous views and mostly great cycle route to be able to stop off at different points including lake beaches for a swim, colonia suiza for artesan shops and food/drinks and a micro brewery BUT would definitely recommend an e-bike as there are a lot of long and in places steep hills. Also be very, very careful on the final few KM as a coach physically ran us off the road onto the gravel resulting in injury, which could have been a lot more serious, bikes on the road are not well respected by all drivers…

Great views.  However…it is NOT an easy route.   There are many very large hills.  Use an e-bike if at all possible.  My half marathon fit son was struggling at times.  You need to be VERY fit to rent a regular bike.  It rooms us closer to 6 hours because we needed more breaks.   What the staff said was “level and easy “ was not so for us.

Do not leave your car out of sight! We got robbed while we stepped out of our rental car. The robbers don't break the glass, just disengage the alarm and open the trunk. They specifically target foreigners with rental cars and are very fast. They don't look suspicious, seem to work in paírs (e.g. young woman and man) with normal looking clothes and act like tourists. If you will stop for the view or take a picture, better to park somewhere where you can see your car anytime. Even if there are people around, do not trust. No one does anything even if they see robbery.

It is worth doing this tour on the first day to have a notion of what to visit after.. we passed by neighborhoods, we went to cerro cathedral, we passed by the famous Llao Llao hotel, and we went to the campanile.

I made the trip on 10/10/24 with the agency Vivencias Travel de Bariloche, the same day I did the Circuito Chico, also did Cerro Catedral, the quiet do the 2 on the same day. The Circuito Chico I did in the morning, was very cool, the Guide super attentive, kind and explained everything in the smallest detail, telling the story of each point we passed and removing our doubts. We climbed the Cerro Campanario and it was simply amazing, the entrance is the part, it was 12,000 pesos, can pay in the hour there, paid in cash, but accept card too. You climb a little hill to the hill, up there it is very cold, because there is a lot of wind, but the view is simply too amazing. There are some photographers who take their photos and then if you want you can buy from them, I found a little affection, but I bought it anyway because I was alone and the photos were cool hahah, but if you followed, I think it makes no sense to spend on it, it's there for your 15,000 pesos (depends on the photographer). Then at the end there is a stop in a church, near the chic hotel Llao Llao, the stay there is mega expensive, but the Guide commented that if you want to spend an afternoon there, you can go because there is a coffee or something of the kind, from which you can buy and walk around the place, if I am not mistaken is about 50 dollars per person (cheaper than a night there).
After all, the walk was amazing, I recommend too.

The Chico circuit is very beautiful with stops at impressive locations, it is worth making this tour. I did with AVC Tourism agency, but could have hired a taxi or rented a car which allows you to do things in your time. The Cerro Campanario has a beautiful view and is worth climbing. The cable car price can be paid in weight, real or dollar and credit card!!!
Beautiful, travel very beautiful places to stop to enjoy and take photos, if you do it Wednesday or Sunday you find the fair of Swiss colony open.

Exclusive tour to stop at points and take pictures , I found it quite dispensable , with a child so it becomes boring . Mehor opt for another type of tour .Even for adults found well without grace. It has the cerro campanario that has a beautiful view but nothing unavoidable.
This place is an amazing place to explore and get submerge in the beaty of this region. Breathtaking views of the panoramic landscape.

Lindoooo! Amazing view!! 
It's worth renting a car!
The.Tours get expensive due to inflation!
There are several lakes! They're easy to find! They're close!

We made in September of 2024 this circuit with the agency experiences , we did in the morning , and is included the climbing in the bell clock and after it begins the Chico circuit.  It was all perfect, very friendly Guide, punctuality .. everything ok .. 
But this circuit can be done by car perfectly and you can include at the end a walk to the brewery Patagonia and a stop in the municipal park Llao Llao ( super easy track ) . So much so that then we rented a car in vivências and we again made this circuit but in our time and we discovered beautiful places that no excursion does. The car we rented was a Sandero for 4 days went off at 45,000 pesos per day with free km. 
I will attach the map of the Chico circuit for those who want to take the ride with rental car. 
We visit the chapel of St. Edward and the mosquito rose shop , which if you want to buy you will leave a kidney . We have the mosquito rose shop in Gramado and it's not that fortune as they charge in Bariloche. 
Obs .. everything is very expensive in Bariloche , the tours , the food , not only in Bariloche but throughout Argentina . Look a lot before you go , the prices are the same as in Europe ... a meal for a couple doesn't go for less than R$300,00 , a simple empanada costs AR$2,200,00 , a 500 gram steak eye costs AR$35,000 ( from for 2 people ) without accompaniment at Tony's Parrila restaurant ( SAN martin ) .  In the case meal for 2 people with soda around AR$ 45,000. 
But in Buenos Aires it is more expensive. Search a lot before you go. Exchange rate at Western Union was AR$ 228.00 .
Wonderful walk. The view from the bell tower is really imperative. The ride on the cable car is a delight. Then this tour includes a city tour. Really very good.

Be very careful in parking the trails to the Roman bridge and hidden lake. They open the rented cars, steal the money from the wallets and leave everything neatly locked as it was so you don't notice in the moment. They take nothing else but cash. When we talked about it among Barilochens, they told us it always happens there. Unfortunate that the municipality does not take care of tourists, if everyone knows what happens there should be a patrol boat. Too bad.
The Chico Circuit in Bariloche is one of the biggest attractions in the city. Breathtaking landscapes emerge at every blink of eye . Nature was capricious with the lake region.

An impossible tour not to do. 
It is advisable to leave Bariloche in the morning and picnic at the side of the lake, beach or stream.
Can be done at any time of year

Beautiful tour. I added the visit to Cerro Catedral, so it was an all-day excursion. I climbed the hill Campanario in aeroilla. It's really wonderful the view. Promotion is paid separately. It's worth it.
Be prepared to keep your mouth open.....of course the weather conditions have to help, but really everything is of immense beauty.

This iconic excursion begins in Puerto Pañuelo, where you will embark on the historic Modesta Victoria, a 1938 naval gem with bronze and wood details that transforms sailing into a journey back in time. During the tour, you will visit the immense Victoria Island, exploring its trails, Puerto Anchorena and Playa del Toro, and then marvel at the Arrayanes Forest on the Quetrihue Peninsula, unique in the world for its cinnamon-colored specimens. It is an essential experience because it combines the majesty of Patagonian nature with the mystique of sailing the most famous lake in the region on a boat of great heritage value.
Nice place. Quiet and beautiful. They didn't have gluten-free alternatives in the cafeteria, so it's best to take. Impeccable bathrooms.
A truly beautiful place: the color of the water, intense green, is of great impact. The ancient trees are majestic and the landscape of the lagoon is enchanting. A visit that leaves you speechless.

The walk through the island is very beautiful, it is worth it, the guide introduced us to the history of the place and how it was the change from private island to a national park and other curiosities about local development.

What a beautiful walk! It is worth seeing Isla Victoria. Wonderful vegetation. We did the tour with the cau cau and the staff were wonderful, especially the Jéssica guide who is very friendly and speaks a great Portuguese.

Wonderful!

It is worth every penny invested in it to stroll, listen to the stories and appreciate the beauty of nature present in this place.

Note 1 million.

We pick up the Cau-cau boat at Porto Pañero at 2 p.m. A stretch of 30 min of navigation to the island and we make a trail that for me was the most interesting point: the Guide Melina told us about the Patagonian peoples and the history of the island, then another stretch of 45 min of navigation to another island we do a wooden boarding trail and the return of +- 1 hour. The view is beautiful, the seagulls arrive near the boat (it is forbidden to feed them as before). We went by rental car and bought in Porto right ( has discount for 4). The Chico circuit passes in front of this Porto (the Porto is in front of the Llau Llau hotel), I suggest to make the Chico circuit before and take advantage of to buy the boat ride that you will do on another day.

Beyond the price, the boarding fee, the entrance to the park, and (optional) the transfer to Puerto Pañuelo, it is a very interesting island, given that it has a lot of history, 100% nature, beach, botanical garden, restaurant. ..question of finding out the departure and arrival times of the boats/catamarans.

Highly recommended adventure experience in Bariloche.

Enjoyable bathing in the lake and dozens of interesting species of trees and plants, to liven up your enjoyment with general culture.
